headline: Apollo economist warns AI agents could trigger a bank run at machine speed
body: Torsten Slok, Apollo's chief economist, wrote in a client note that AI agents could sweep household cash out of checking accounts paying around 0.1 percent into fintech accounts yielding 3.3 to 5 percent, all at once. He said that could drain banks of the cheap deposits they rely on to fund lending, turning slow deposit flight into a synchronized, machine-speed run.
note: Digital bank runs so far have depended on people panicking together. An agent doing exactly what it was told, chasing yield continuously, does not panic, it just executes, so a rate gap regulators have long tolerated now reads as a standing vulnerability rather than background noise.
